headline: Healthy habits keep older minds sharp

sources.title: Lifestyle Program Improves Brain Health in Latin America
From the Alzheimer's Association International Conference 2026: Lifestyle Program Improves Brain Health Among Older Adults at Risk for Dementia Across Latin America
A Two-Year Lifestyle Program Helped Older Adults Sharpen Their Memory

chunks.text: Doctors have long wondered how people can keep their minds sharp as they grow older. Now, a large study across Latin America has {{set out}} to answer that question. Scientists {{teamed up}} with older adults in 11 countries and {{rolled out}} a two year program to protect memory and slow mental [[decline]]. The results were shared at a major [[dementia]] conference in July 2026.

chunks.text: More than 1,000 adults, aged 60 to 77, {{signed up}} for the study. Half of them followed a strict plan with [[supervised]] exercise four times a week, healthy [[nutrition]] based on local foods, computer games for the brain, and regular [[cardiovascular]] checks. To make it fun, the team added popular dances like salsa and tango. The people in this group had to {{stick to}} the plan and {{keep up}} their new habits for two whole years.

chunks.text: The other half {{took part}} in a lighter version. They got only general health advice at four short meetings and had to manage mostly on their own. After two years, the difference was clear. The structured group improved their [[cognition]] about 55 percent more than the [[flexible]] group, and those who worked alone often {{fell behind}} on tests of memory. Many of them {{ended up}} with smaller gains in thinking.

verbs.correct: To be one of the people doing an activity

chunks.text: Experts {{point out}} that structure and social support make a real difference. Meeting in groups kept people [[motivated]] and helped them worry less. The scientists say a healthy lifestyle can help {{ward off}} memory loss and may {{keep on}} protecting the brain for years. They hope more countries will bring this kind of [[affordable]] program to people who want to age well.

tf.s: Scientists rolled out a two year program in 11 Latin American countries.
tf.why: Scientists rolled out the program across 11 countries in Latin America.

tf.s: Adults in the lighter group often fell behind on memory tests.
tf.why: Those who worked mostly alone often fell behind on tests of memory.

tf.s: The structured group only had to keep up their new habits for a few weeks.
tf.why: They had to keep up their new habits for two whole years, not a few weeks.

tf.s: More than 1,000 adults signed up for the two year study.
tf.why: More than 1,000 adults aged 60 to 77 signed up for the study.

tf.s: Experts point out that staying alone at home works better than meeting in groups.
tf.why: Experts point out that structure and social support in groups make a real difference.

tf.s: The scientists say a healthy lifestyle cannot help ward off memory loss.
tf.why: They say a healthy lifestyle can help ward off memory loss and protect the brain.
